Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) stock is up about 1% in Wednesday’s premarket session as investors head into the open with steady risk appetite. Nasdaq futures are down 0.01%, while S&P 500 futures have gained 0.11%.

Amazon Expands AI Shopping Push

In other news, the company blocked Meta Platforms Inc.’s (NASDAQ:META) Muse AI agent from shopping on Amazon.com. Amazon requires automated systems to identify themselves and stop accessing its services when requested.

At the same time, Amazon is expanding its own AI shopping ecosystem. The company combined Rufus and Alexa+ into Alexa for Shopping. The service can compare products, track prices, build shopping carts and automate purchases.

Amazon has also challenged Perplexity AI over its Comet shopping agent, alleging unauthorized access to customer accounts.

Technical Analysis

Amazon is trading in a key decision zone. The stock is hovering just above its 20-day, 50-day and 100-day simple moving averages, which are clustered near $255 to $256.

Meanwhile, Amazon remains 6.7% above its 200-day SMA of $240.53. That keeps the longer-term trend constructive despite choppy near-term trading.

Momentum is neutral. The stock’s relative strength index stands at 48.86. An RSI near 50 suggests neither buyers nor sellers have clear control.

The moving-average picture is also mixed. The 20-day SMA remains below the 50-day SMA, signaling a weaker near-term trend. However, the 50-day SMA remains above the 200-day SMA following a golden cross in May.

Amazon reached a 52-week high in August after rebounding from a July swing low. Recent trading suggests the stock is consolidating after that midyear rally.

Key resistance stands near $267.50, an area where rallies could face selling pressure. Support sits near $226, a prior demand zone defended by buyers earlier this year.

Analyst Outlook

The stock carries a Buy consensus rating and an average price forecast of $331.48.

Wells Fargo maintained an Overweight rating on Sept. 3 and raised its price target to $338. Rosenblatt maintained a Buy rating with a $335 target on Aug. 20. UBS maintained a Buy rating and raised its target to $318 on July 31.

Benzinga Edge Rankings

The stock has a Momentum score of 75.59 and a Growth score of 94.02. Its Quality score stands at 58.33, while its Value score is 57.92.

The scores point to a growth-led profile with relatively strong momentum. Value and quality rank closer to the middle of the broader market.

Top ETF Exposure

Amazon carries significant weight in several exchange-traded funds.

The company represents 9.78% of the First Trust Dow Jones Internet Index Fund (NYSE:FDN), 9.13% of the Franklin Focused Dynamic Growth ETF (NASDAQ:FFOG) and 8.71% of the Eagle Capital Select Equity ETF (NYSE:EAGL).

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) criticized the Trump administration’s silence on artificial intelligence (AI) risks, pointing out potential conflicts of interest.

Schumer took to X on Tuesday to express his concern over the lack of response to his call for a classified Senate briefing on AI risks. This includes cybersecurity and the flow of AI chips and manufacturing equipment to China.

“We’ve heard nothing but crickets over a week…” he wrote.

He suggested that the Trump family’s significant AI-related investments might be influencing the administration’s stance.

“Maybe Trump’s not worried because his family has hundreds of millions (if not billions) tied up in the AI economy,” added Schumer.

Read Also: Jensen Huang Says AI CEOs May Have 'Ulterior', Maybe 'Political' Reasons For AI Doomsday Warnings: 'Go and Read Between The Lines'

Schumer Pushes Back On Trump’s AI Stance

Schumer’s post comes a week after he and Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) pushed back against Trump’s dismissal of AI safety concerns. Schumer emphasized that the U.S. cannot afford to ignore the potential dangers of AI, regardless of the intelligence of the current president.

Earlier this month, Schumer called for an All-Senators classified briefing for all senators on AI risks, citing warnings from an Anthropic researcher about the dangers of pursuing artificial superintelligence. Schumer urged the Trump administration to explain its frontier AI testing framework, efforts to prevent AI chips and semiconductor equipment from reaching China, and plans to protect the U.S. from AI-enabled cyberattacks.

On Tuesday, Trump said the Justice Department could intervene if AI companies create serious problems, while opposing new regulations he believes could hinder U.S. innovation. At the U.N., Trump also said federal documents would use the term “Super Intelligence” instead of “Artificial Intelligence.”

Trump’s Trades Target AI And Tech

Trump disclosed more than 20,000 stock trades over the past year, with investment disclosures released in May, July and August. The holdings were heavily concentrated in AI infrastructure, cloud computing and consumer technology companies.

Some of the companies that formed a part of his trades are Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), Oracle Corp. (NYSE:ORCL), Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN), Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD).

Great Hill Capital Chairman Thomas Hayes suggested Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) should acquire PayPal Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:PYPL) for $90 billion, stating the deal could save Meta “5-10 years” in building a “WeChat super-app” ahead of Elon Musk‘s Xmoney.

Strategic Advantage Over Xmoney

Writing as a PayPal shareholder, Hayes posted his acquisition thesis following a new payment partnership between the two technology companies.

Hayes argued that Meta Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg could “beat him to the punch” against Musk, who is currently trying to build Xmoney from the ground up. A $90 billion acquisition price—representing approximately a 7% free cash flow yield—would be “highly accretive immediately” whether structured as a cash, stock, or combination deal.

Hayes added that $90 billion is “a price shareholders would accept,” noting a partial stock transaction allows PayPal investors to “participate in additional upside” in what he termed a “win-win” deal.

Read Also: Buying SOFI Is Like Buying 'AMD or Nvidia' at the Bottom: Strategists Highlight Bold Bull Case for SoFi Technologies

Data Monetization and Ad Revenue

While Meta dominates targeted advertising, Hayes stated that PayPal holds the superior dataset on consumer purchases and intent. Drawing comparisons to Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN), which built a $68 billion ad business with a 70% margin based on purchase history data, Hayes projected that PayPal’s dataset, paired with Meta, could be worth at least “half as much as Amazon’s ad business.”

Under this valuation framework, he estimated the payback period on a $90 billion purchase price would take three to four years.

AI Partnership Background and Market Reaction

The buyout proposal follows PayPal’s announcement of a partnership with Meta to enable customers to shop and check out using Muse, Meta’s personal AI agent, across PayPal’s global merchant base.

The arrangement expands an existing relationship through Meta Pay, where users link accounts via Meta’s Accounts Center and set default payment methods such as PayPal Balance or PayPal Credit.

How Has PYPL Performed in 2026?

Price Action: At the last check, the PYPL stock was trading 1.15% higher in premarket on Wednesday. It was down 21.85% over the last year, 9.40% year-to-date, and 14.07% over the last month. The stock closed 0.51% higher at $52.89 on Tuesday.

Benzinga’s Edge Stock Rankings indicate that PYPL maintains a weak price trend in the short and long terms but a strong trend in the medium term, with a poor growth score.

Insights From Analysts

In his commentary, Professor Jeremy Siegel presents a balanced outlook on the U.S. economy and stock market, highlighting underlying growth alongside key risks from rising bond yields.

Siegel notes that “economic growth remains very strong,” supported by robust retail sales and solid GDP expectations, though persistent inflation has led the Fed to tighten policy. While he expects the Fed’s next rate increase in December, he stresses that long-term Treasury yields—not short-term rate hikes—pose the primary test for equities.

With the 10-year Treasury yield hovering near 5%, Siegel observes that “if yields stabilize below 5%, equities can continue to grind higher,” but a decisive move above that threshold makes further market advances far more difficult.

Regarding artificial intelligence, Siegel remains optimistic about its long-term potential, though he cautions that short-term demand for computing power is creating temporary inflationary pressures.

He believes AI will ultimately boost economy-wide productivity and lower costs, likening the current environment to “Robert Solow’s famous observation in the 1980s… that computers could be seen everywhere except in the productivity statistics,” before gains eventually materialized. Overall, he views equities as resilient, provided bond yields remain contained.

Rigetti Computing Inc. (NASDAQ:RGTI) shares are trading higher Wednesday in sympathy with IonQ Inc. (NYSE:IONQ) after that company announced it will bring the first quantum processor to NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA)‘s Accelerated Quantum Research Center.

  • Rigetti Computing shares are powering higher. What’s behind RGTI gains?

Quantum System to Power Hybrid Computing Research at NVIDIA Center

IonQ said it will be the first on-premise quantum computing deployment at the NVIDIA Accelerated Quantum Research Center, a facility designed to help scale quantum processors into a new class of accelerated quantum supercomputers. As part of the partnership, an IonQ Superion 256 system will be installed at the facility and directly linked with an NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 system via NVIDIA NVQLink, with workloads orchestrated by NVIDIA’s open CUDA-Q platform. The joint research program will focus on hybrid software development and large-scale system prototyping, targeting applications including portfolio optimization and risk modeling in financial services, materials science, and computational chemistry for drug discovery.

“Deploying our Superion 256 into cutting-edge environments, such as NVIDIA’s NVAQC will lead to developments allowing our partners to benefit from our scalable architecture and robust manufacturability,” said Niccolo de Masi, IonQ Chairman and CEO. “We see this as the beginning of an exciting era of hybrid quantum-classical computing.”

“Every supercomputer will become a quantum supercomputer,” said Timothy Costa, Vice President and General Manager for Quantum at NVIDIA. “As the first quantum processor to sit alongside the NVAQC’s GB200 NVL72 system, IonQ’s Superion 256 will help make breakthroughs allowing the global ecosystem to integrate QPUs with AI infrastructure.”

IonQ introduced its sixth-generation Superion platform on September 8, with the Superion 256 available to order now and first customer deliveries expected in 2027. Installation at NVAQC is scheduled for next year.

Why RGTI Is Moving

Rigetti is one of IonQ’s closest publicly traded peers in the quantum computing space, and the two stocks frequently trade in tandem on sector-wide news, since developments that validate quantum computing’s commercial viability or deepen its integration with AI infrastructure tend to lift investor sentiment across the entire industry rather than just the company involved.

Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) stock edged higher in Wednesday premarket trading as investors continued to favor large-cap technology stocks.

The move came despite a softer broader market. Nasdaq futures fell 0.24%, while S&P 500 futures slipped 0.09%.

Analyst sentiment also remained upbeat Wednesday, with KeyBanc and Cantor Fitzgerald raising their price forecasts on Meta while maintaining Overweight ratings.

Meta Tests ‘Human Concierge’ For Muse AI

Separately, Meta tested a “human concierge” feature for its new Muse AI assistant, using contractors to handle some phone calls placed through the service, Reuters reported.

Meta enabled the feature for half of its employees last week, according to an internal post cited by Reuters. Under the test, Muse could hand a request to a trained human agent, who would place and handle the call. Employees could opt out.

Some Meta employees raised concerns that human agents could gain access to sensitive information during calls. Internal posts cited by Reuters warned that information could be shared unintentionally with contractors working in call centers.

Meta has since rolled back the feature.

Technical Analysis

Meta has held above its recent breakout area. Traders are watching whether that strength can continue as broader market sentiment remains cautious.

The stock is trading well above key moving averages. It is 16.4% above its 20-day simple moving average of $633.06. It is also 17.9% above its 200-day SMA of $625.11.

That setup supports the longer-term bullish trend. However, it also leaves the stock vulnerable to a pullback if momentum fades.

The 20-day SMA is above the 50-day SMA, another positive technical signal. However, the 50-day SMA remains below the 200-day average following a “death cross” in December 2025.

Meanwhile, Meta’s relative strength index stands at 75.68. An RSI above 70 is generally considered overbought. That suggests the stock could be due for consolidation after its recent rally.

Resistance sits near $744. A breakout above that level could support further upside. Support is near $595 if the stock sees a deeper pullback.

Analyst Outlook

Meta carries a Buy consensus rating with an average price forecast of $793.08.

KeyBanc raised its price target to $900 from a previous level Wednesday and maintained an Overweight rating. Cantor Fitzgerald also maintained an Overweight rating and raised its target to $860. Bank of America maintained a Buy rating and $810 price target Tuesday.

The stock trades at about 27.7 times earnings.

Benzinga Edge Rankings

Meta scores strongly on growth, momentum and quality in the Benzinga Edge rankings.

Its Growth score stands at 79.72, while Momentum is 78.77 and Quality is 75.93. Value is lower at 47.03.

The readings point to a stock supported by growth and momentum, although its valuation profile is less compelling.

ETF Exposure

The Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF (NYSE:IGPT) has an 8.43% weighting in Meta. The Natixis Loomis Sayles Focused Growth ETF (NYSE:LSGR) has an 8.12% weighting, while the Invesco Nasdaq Internet ETF (NASDAQ:PNQI) has a 7.89% weighting.

news.author: Erica Kollmann
news.content:
IonQ Inc. (NYSE:IONQ) gave quantum stocks a lift Wednesday morning after the company said it built and tested what it calls the industry’s first end-to-end, real-time quantum error-correction decoder running on a single standard CPU.

  • IONQ stock is climbing. See the chart and price action here.

IonQ stock traded at $45.60 premarket, up 11.93% from Tuesday’s $40.74 close. Even with the jump, shares sit about 46% below their 52-week high of $84.64, according to Benzinga Pro market data. 

What IonQ Showed

Error correction is critical in the race toward fault-tolerant machines, and physical qubits are fragile and pick up environmental noise. The classical computers that find and fix those errors can get overwhelmed. When that happens, the quantum system has to pause while decoding catches up.

IonQ said its dual-decoder architecture handled benchmark circuits simulating up to 408 logical qubits and more than 31.5 million quantum operations. Under standard noise, it added as little as 0.02% “stretch” time, so decoding barely slowed the computation. 

Read Also: Meta Stock Runs Overbought Into Connect — Wall Street Still Targets $800+

“Successfully validating real-time decoding across hundreds of logical qubits and over millions of logical operations is an important milestone. Moreover, the fact that our decoder runs on a single CPU provides a practical path to commercial-scale fault-tolerant quantum computing,” said Nicolas Delfosse, quantum research lead at IonQ.

The company tied the result to its Walking Cat architecture. It also linked the result to a roadmap that goes beyond 256 physical qubits toward platforms controlling thousands.

The Group Follows

The bid has spread to other quantum pure plays. Rigetti Computing Inc. (NASDAQ:RGTI) rose 4.48% to $17.26 premarket. D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NYSE:QBTS) gained 4.95% to $18.43, and Quantum Computing Inc. (NASDAQ:QUBT) added 4.18% to $9.46.

The newer names also joined Wednesday’s move. Infleqtion Inc. (NYSE:INFQ) rose 4.41% to $14.68 premarket, and Horizon Quantum Holdings Ltd. (NASDAQ:HQ) climbed 4.26% to $16.41. 

Xanadu Quantum Technologies Ltd. (NASDAQ:XNDU) lagged with a 1.73% gain to $5.88. It closed Tuesday at $5.78, down about 22% on the day, as its post-IPO lockup period expired. 

Larger players moved less, with International Business Machines Corp. (NYSE:IBM) edging up 0.92% and NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) slipping 0.55% in Wednesday’s premarket session.  

See More: Top Momentum Stocks

Why Traders Care

Error correction has sparked rallies before. In April, quantum names surged after Nvidia released Ising, a family of open-source AI models aimed partly at quantum error correction and calibration. IonQ and D-Wave each climbed more than 50% that week.

Rosenblatt Securities analyst John McPeake said quantum companies gain legitimacy by hitting technical milestones on their public roadmaps, according to the Wall Street Journal. Many of those roadmaps target fault tolerance by the end of the decade. 

Read Also: Micron's 343% Growth Boom Is Already Over, I/O Fund Says — Now Comes the Hard Part

news.author: Surbhi Jain
news.content:
Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) has something new to show investors after years of pouring billions into artificial intelligence: consumers appear to want the product. Muse has raced up app charts since its Sept. 8 launch, helping push Meta shares more than 20% higher. But Jensen Investment Management recently sold its Meta position over concerns about the returns on the company’s escalating AI investment — putting that decision under a new spotlight.

"META validated an important part of our original thesis," Allen Bond, Managing Director and Portfolio Manager at Jensen Investment Management, told Benzinga in an exclusive email interview. But he said Meta’s subsequent acceleration in capital spending and R&D was "greater than we anticipated," while the returns on much of that additional investment remain uncertain. "Our sale reflected this change in incremental ROIC," Bond said, "rather than deterioration in META’s high-quality core business."

Muse Changes the AI Debate

The early traction has quickly made Muse the centerpiece of Meta’s AI story.

Early adoption has given investors plenty to celebrate. Apptopia estimates Muse generated 2.8 million global installs during its first 12 days, while its U.S. and Canada iOS downloads outpaced ChatGPT’s comparable early mobile launch, reported TechCrunch. Muse has also reached No. 1 on the U.S. App Store.

Meta shares have responded accordingly. The stock gained more than 20% since Muse launched, with the stock’s rally adding about $200 billion in market value as investors began viewing the agent as a potential new revenue engine.

But Bond’s assessment goes beyond whether Meta has built a hit. The issue for Jensen is what happens to the economics as Meta’s AI investment gets larger. While AI has already demonstrated benefits for "user experience, ad targeting and monetization," the acceleration in capex and R&D means Meta now has to generate enough additional economic value to justify the expanding investment.

Read Also: EXCLUSIVE: Father of AGI Warns Investors May Be Mispricing Meta's AI Moat

Investors Need More Than Downloads

For Bond, the evidence of sufficient AI returns would have to show up in the financial statements.

"Evidence of sufficient AI returns would include sustained revenue benefits," he said, followed ultimately by "a return toward historical free-cash-flow and margin profiles" across the major hyperscalers as investment growth normalizes.

And Bond sees several variables that make the return equation difficult to forecast. He points to "the magnitude and duration of the capex cycle," AI-model monetization, political pushback and "rapid improvements in chip efficiency and technology."

The ROI Test

But Bond’s framework shifts the investor question from "Will people use Muse?" to "Will the economics justify what Meta is spending to build it?"

For META, downloads may have fueled the rally; sustained revenue, cash flow and margins will determine whether the AI investment can ultimately earn its keep.

Read Also: Meta vs. Amazon: The AI E-Commerce Battle

news.author: Daragh Thomas
news.content:
Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) told employees that some tests showed human callers handling requests for its Muse AI agent could achieve success rates of 95%-98%, higher than AI-only calls, according to internal posts reviewed by Reuters.

Meta tested the human layer with employees and has since rolled it back. The company did not disclose the AI-only success rate, saying only that it was lower.

• Meta Platforms stock is showing positive momentum. What’s the outlook for META shares?

Humans Prove More Reliable Than Muse

Meta began testing Muse’s phone-calling capability with employees in August. The agent can call businesses to book appointments, check whether products are in stock and get quotes on a user’s behalf.

Some calls struggled. One employee said an insurance company repeatedly hung up when Muse disclosed that it was AI, Reuters reported.

Meta later enabled a "human concierge" for half of its employees. Muse could hand a request to a trained contractor, who placed the call and worked through the task.

The episode highlights a problem better AI models may not solve. Even if an agent can handle the task, the person or business on the other end may simply refuse to deal with it.

Meta rolled back the experiment after another employee said a contractor made a racist reference while negotiating his cable bill. A Meta executive apologized and said the contractor would no longer work on Meta projects.

Meta said employee feedback on the test was "overwhelmingly positive" and that it would launch the human-assisted feature publicly only when ready and with proper disclosures.

Meta Has Faced This Before

The experiment echoes Facebook’s M assistant, launched in 2015 to make reservations, shop and perform other errands.

M also relied on humans to complete tasks its AI could not handle. Media reports later estimated people carried out around 70% of its requests before Facebook shut the project down in 2018.

See More: Top Quality Stocks

Wall Street Bets on Muse

The reliability gap matters because Muse is becoming an increasingly important part of Meta’s effort to turn years of heavy AI spending into a major consumer business.

Investor and YouTuber Joseph Carlson said Muse has given Meta shareholders "a positive story, something to latch on to, a story to anchor onto." He argued the product has helped change sentiment around the company even before analysts materially changed earnings estimates.

Meta shares have climbed more than 20% since Muse launched Sept. 8, adding over $200 billion in market value. Muse recorded 2.8 million downloads in its first 12 days.

Polymarket traders currently give Meta a 74% chance of touching $760 before the end of September, with about $70,000 wagered on the market.

JPMorgan said Muse could become the most widely used consumer AI app since ChatGPT, while Jefferies estimated it could generate $10.8 billion in annualized revenue if it reaches 1 billion users by the end of 2027 and converts 3% to paid plans.

news.author: Daragh Thomas
news.content:
Former Fidelity fund manager George Noble says the artificial intelligence boom looks like "dot-com and subprime all merged in one," warning that massive spending on AI may fail to generate adequate returns.

"Show me the ROI," Noble told "Big Short" investor Steve Eisman on The Real Eisman Playbook. Noble said funding could eventually dry up if returns fail to justify the amount of capital being deployed.

The warning comes as AI stocks rally again. Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) crossed $1 trillion in market value for the first time Monday, while a semiconductor-led rally pushed the Nasdaq 100 to a three-month high.

AI Can Win While Investors Lose

Noble pointed to the dot-com era, when bullish forecasts for internet adoption proved broadly correct even as companies building the infrastructure collapsed.

Internet traffic subsequently exploded, he said, but that "didn’t stop Global Crossing and all the rest of them from going bankrupt."

"The point is AI is set up to fail," Noble said, arguing that the capital being deployed may ultimately outrun the returns available to investors.

The financing burden is also growing. Goldman Sachs expects hyperscaler debt issuance to reach a record $420 billion in 2027, up 60% from 2026 estimates, Reuters reported.

Eisman Flags Nvidia Customer Concentration

Eisman said circular financing in AI "kind of drives me crazy," though he added it would matter far less if OpenAI and Anthropic became highly profitable.

Eisman also pointed to Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), noting that five direct customers accounted for about 70% of the chipmaker’s accounts receivable at the end of its latest quarter.

Eisman called the figure "very frightening."

Noble estimated roughly 70% of hyperscaler AI revenue comes from OpenAI and Anthropic, warning that trouble at OpenAI could reverberate through the ecosystem.

"Totally agree," Eisman replied.

Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT) has offered evidence that AI-related cloud demand extends beyond OpenAI and Anthropic.

The company said nearly 90% of Microsoft Cloud revenue in fiscal 2026 came from customers outside frontier-model companies, while its contracted commercial revenue backlog excluding OpenAI still grew 25%.

Prediction Market Sees a Bust as Unlikely

Prediction traders are not yet pricing Noble’s scenario as imminent.

A Polymarket contract with nearly $3 million traded puts the chance of an AI-industry downturn by Dec. 31 at about 11%. However, the growing financing web linking AI suppliers, customers and investors has raised questions about how much of the boom depends on capital continuing to flow.

That gets to the heart of Noble’s argument: being right about the technology does not necessarily mean investors are paying the right price to build it.

Image: Shutterstock

Read Also: S&P 500 Will ‘Easily’ Top 8,000 Before Historic Crash, ‘Black Swan’ Fund Manager Says
news.headline: AI Boom Is ‘Dot-Com and Subprime All Merged in One,’ Former Fidelity Manager Tells Steve Eisman

news.author: Piero Cingari
news.content:
Homebuilder stocks had one of their best days in months on Tuesday. By Wednesday morning, the mortgage data served a cold shower.

The Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) reported that the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate had risen to 7.12% in the week ending Sept. 18.

The iShares U.S. Home Construction ETF (NYSE:ITB) fell 1.36% in early trading on Wednesday, after gaining 3.2% on Tuesday.

Mortgage Rates Hit Highest Level Since 2024

The average contract rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage is now at its highest level since May 2024.

Mortgage rates have now risen by more than 100 basis points since the Iran war began in late February.

On a $400,000 loan, a one-point rise in the rate adds roughly $265 to the monthly payment.

Total mortgage applications fell 1.5%, the third weekly decline in a row. Refinancing applications dropped 2.6%, and purchase applications fell 0.8%.

Refinance demand is now 62% lower than a year ago and at its weakest since February 2025.

Purchase applications are down 11% from a year earlier.

Meanwhile, borrowers are taking more risk.

Some buyers are switching to adjustable-rate mortgages (ARMs). An ARM carries a lower starting rate that can reset higher later, so the borrower takes on the risk that rates keep rising.

“With fixed rates much higher, more borrowers opted for ARMs, with the ARM share reaching 9.8%, as rates for 5/1 ARMs were more than a percentage point lower than those for fixed rate loans,” said Mike Fratantoni, senior vice president and chief economist at the MBA.

Why Mortgage Rates Follow the 30-Year Treasury

Lenders price 30-year mortgages off the 30-year Treasury yield, which is the interest rate the government pays to borrow for 30 years.

When that yield rises, lenders’ funding costs rise. As a result, they charge home buyers more.

The 30-year yield rose 2 basis points to 5.32% on Wednesday morning. It hit 5.42% on Sept. 10, its highest level since 2007.

Earlier this month, the Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 basis points and signaled more hikes could follow.

Several other Fed officials have also sounded hawkish, which strengthened expectations of further tightening.

Yet, economists indicate that the bulk of the increase in long-dated Treasury yields reflects inflation and debt-related concerns in Washington.

Read Also: Trump's Diesel Ban Comes With A Bigger Bill at The Pump

Who Feels Higher Rates Most

Homebuilders feel the effect first. Higher rates shrink the pool of buyers who can qualify for a loan. For this reason, builders often pay to lower buyers’ rates, which cuts into their profit margins.

Mortgage lenders depend on loan volume. Fewer refinancings mean fewer loans to sell.

Home-improvement retailers and real estate brokers depend on housing turnover.

Fewer home sales mean fewer renovations and fewer commissions.

5 Housing Stocks Taking the Hit

The selling on Wednesday morning is concentrated in the stocks most exposed to new loans and first-time buyers. Meanwhile, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY) is down 0.32%.

1. KB Home (NYSE:KBH) is down 0.82% at $48.24. It is the biggest decline in the group. KB Home builds mostly entry-level homes, so its buyers are the ones most likely to stop qualifying for a loan when rates rise. The stock is 28.1% below its February high.

2. Rocket Companies Inc. (NYSE:RKT) is down 2.16% at $12.46. Rocket Companies earns money on every mortgage it makes, and refinance demand is now 62% lower than a year ago. The stock hit a 52-week low on Monday and trades 47.7% below its January high.

3. Compass Inc. (NYSE:COMP) is down 2.95% at $9.39, after falling 4.5% on Tuesday. As a real estate broker, Compass earns commissions only when homes change hands. As a result, fewer purchase applications mean fewer deals.

4. UWM Holdings Corp. (NYSE:UWMC) is down 2.75% at $1.24. Like Rocket Companies, UWM Holdings depends on loan volume. The stock is 80.7% below its high from a year ago.

5. Lennar Corp. (NYSE:LEN) is down 0.41% at $82.70, after jumping 6.4% on Tuesday. Lennar touched a 52-week low of $75.70 on Sept. 18. It remains 37.9% below its December high.

Read Also: Micron Earnings Are Set for a 10x Jump: The Stock Is Still the Cheapest in Tech

IonQ, Inc. (NYSE:IONQ) shares are trading higher on Wednesday. The company said its Superion 256 quantum computer will be the first quantum processing unit installed at NVIDIA’s Accelerated Quantum Research Center (NVAQC).

NVAQC is a facility focused on integrating quantum processors with accelerated computing.

Install Superion 256 At NVIDIA Quantum Research Center

The deployment will connect IonQ’s full-stack quantum systems with NVIDIA’s AI infrastructure to advance large-scale quantum computing.

Under the partnership, IonQ will install a Superion 256 system at NVAQC and connect it directly to an NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 system through NVIDIA NVQLink, with workloads managed by the open NVIDIA CUDA-Q platform.

Read Also: Rigetti Stock Rises as IonQ-NVIDIA Deal Lifts Quantum Computing Sector

The joint research will focus on hybrid software development, large-scale system prototyping and quantum-GPU co-design, with applications including portfolio optimization and risk modeling, materials science and computational chemistry for drug discovery.

Notably, IonQ launched its sixth-generation Superion platform on September 8, 2026. The Superion 256 is available to order, with first customer deliveries expected in 2027, while its NVAQC installation is also scheduled for next year.

Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Milestone

On Tuesday, the company disclosed a milestone in fault-tolerant quantum computing, with researchers developing and successfully testing.

The company stated it is the industry’s first end-to-end, real-time quantum error correction decoder running on a single standard, commercially available CPU.

IONQ Technical Outlook: Key Levels And Momentum

With the stock at $45.29, it’s trading 15.2% above its 20-day SMA ($39.07) and 14.7% above its 50-day SMA ($39.24), but still 4.5% below its 100-day SMA ($47.13) — a setup that often turns the mid-to-high $40s into a "prove it" zone.

Momentum looks more like consolidation than a breakout chase: RSI is 53.29, which signals the move isn’t especially stretched yet (RSI is a gauge of how overheated or oversold price action is). The bigger-picture trend is still trying to repair itself after the death cross in August (50-day SMA below the 200-day SMA), even though price is now back above the 200-day SMA ($43.78).

  • Key Resistance: $48.00 — a nearby round-number area that can act as a stall point as price approaches the 100-day SMA zone
  • Key Support: $37.00 — a prior buyer-defense area that sits well below current levels, leaving room for volatility if the premarket pop fades

IONQ Earnings Preview And Analyst Price Targets

Looking further out, the next major catalyst for the stock arrives with the November 4, 2026 (estimated) earnings report.

  • EPS Estimate: Loss of 72 cents (Down from a loss of 17 cents from the same quarter last year)
  • Revenue Estimate: $143.50 million (Up from $39.87 million from the same quarter last year)

Analyst Consensus & Recent Actions: The stock carries a Buy rating with an average price forecast of $67.75. Recent analyst moves include:

  • Wedbush: Outperform (Maintains Target to $75.00) (Sept. 22)
  • Mizuho: Outperform (Lowers Target to $52.00) (Sept. 9)
  • Rosenblatt: Buy (Maintains Target to $100.00) (Sept. 9)

Top ETFs Holding IonQ Stock

  • Corgi Quantum Computing 2x Daily ETF (NASDAQ:XQTM): 15.34% Weight
  • WisdomTree Quantum Computing Fund ETF (NASDAQ:WQTM): 5.55% Weight
  • State Street SPDR FactSet Innovative Technology ETF (NYSE:XITK): 1.70% Weight

Significance: Because IONQ carries such a heavy weight in these funds, any significant inflows or outflows for these ETFs will likely force automatic buying or selling of the stock.

news.author: Daragh Thomas
news.content:
Artificial intelligence companies may be building far more compute than it ultimately needs, according to Tyler Saltsman, CEO of EdgeRunner AI.

The compute being built is “a little overkill,” Saltsman told Benzinga. “I think what will happen is AI will become too expensive, and all of this data center demand will start to drop.”

Saltsman expects AI’s future to consist of specialized models working together rather than a single enormous system trying to do everything.

‘The World Doesn’t Need AGI’

“Future intelligence isn’t going to be one big mega-model,” he added. “The world doesn’t need AGI, what it needs is domain-specific GPT-4 level models.”

Saltsman, whose company sells specialized on-device AI models, said one EdgeRunner military assistant can run at roughly 4 billion parameters using 8GB to 16GB of video memory on consumer-grade hardware.

After training in a data center, EdgeRunner compresses its models so they can run directly on a device without repeatedly sending requests to the cloud.

Saltsman said that approach could “completely undercut” the large AI companies’ bottom line by removing recurring per-token charges.

He also argued that competition from open-source models helps explain recent calls from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman to slow frontier AI development.

“Open source is catching up, and it threatens their business model,” Saltsman said.

Why EdgeRunner Says Smaller Military AI Works Better

EdgeRunner builds smaller, military-specific AI models designed to run directly on soldiers’ devices without an internet connection. Saltsman says training the models on military doctrine, terminology and use cases can make them more reliable on battlefield tasks than general-purpose LLMs.

He pointed to a recent incident in which a faulty AI-assisted intelligence report wrongly identified a Chinese ship as carrying nuclear-related components, nearly triggering a U.S. military operation. EdgeRunner reduced error rates by 37% in one training run using data from the Army’s Artificial Intelligence Integration Center, Saltsman said.

Nvidia Still Wins, but AI Compute Could Shift

Saltsman stopped short of predicting weaker demand for Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), praising its chips and CUDA software platform. Instead, he expects computing power to shift as companies match models more closely to individual tasks.

He compared using massive frontier models for military mission planning to firing a $2 million Patriot missile at a $20,000 drone.

“If you’re just using these powerful mega-models for mission planning, it can be overkill,” Saltsman said.

Prediction-market traders remain bullish on Nvidia. Polymarket gives the chipmaker a 78% chance of ending 2026 as the world’s largest company, compared with Apple (15%), on roughly $7.5 million in trading volume.

Benzinga reported Wednesday that McKinsey found the same task can cost up to 30 times more depending on the AI agent used.

news.author: Parshwa Turakhiya
news.content:
President Donald Trump’s stock accounts sold Strategy (NASDAQ:MSTR) shares in June, bought back in late July, and the stock has since climbed 83%.

What the Filing Shows

A federal ethics filing posted September 22 shows the accounts sold Strategy shares worth $16,002 to $65,000 combined on June 23 and June 24, just before the stock hit $81.81 two days later, its lowest point of the summer. 

A third sale followed on July 8, worth $1,001 to $15,000, before the accounts reversed course and started buying.

They purchased $1,001 to $15,000 of Strategy on July 24 and a much larger $50,001 to $100,000 on July 27. 

Strategy closed at $91.67 on July 24 and $167.33 on September 22, an 83% gain flagged by Quiver Quantitative, which tracks politicians’ trades. 

The larger July 27 purchase, made at a $98.65 close, now sits up roughly 70%. Since Strategy holds the largest corporate Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) position in the world, its stock tends to move in step with crypto prices, which helps explain the timing of the run.

Why This Draws Extra Attention

Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Massachusetts) and Rep. Robert Garcia (D-California) sent a letter on August 12 demanding answers about whether Trump’s stock trading created conflicts between his personal finances and official duties. 

They cited more than 14,000 reported trades worth up to $1.06 billion in 2025, and another 3,555 trades worth up to $500 million in the first three months of 2026.

The lawmakers flagged 30 example trades tied to government decisions or presidential endorsements, including:

  • Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) — purchased a week before eased chip export restrictions
  • Coinbase (NASDAQ:COIN) — purchased the day before Trump met the company’s CEO and publicly backed crypto
  • Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR) — purchased before Trump praised the stock ahead of a $300 million Agriculture Department deal

The Trump Organization has denied any role in directing the trades, stating independent financial institutions manage the accounts without advance notice. 

Warren and Garcia called that explanation insufficient and set an August 28 deadline for detailed answers, aiming to inform potential legislation barring presidents from owning individual stocks.

MSTR Price Analysis: Key Levels to Watch

MSTR trades flat Wednesday, after pulling back from an intraday high of $169. 

The broader trend stays bullish, with price holding above the 200-day EMA at $152.43 after clearing the multi-month descending trendline last week. 

The Supertrend flipped bullish back in August near $100 and now trails support at $139.84.

Key levels for MSTR:

  • $171.19 — recent high
  • $152.43 — 200-day EMA, key support below

news.author: Daragh Thomas
news.content:
AI agents that shop, book trips and transact could pressure Booking Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:BKNG) and Intuit Inc. (NASDAQ:INTU) while benefiting Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) and Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT), according to investing commentator Joseph Carlson.

"Automation is not the biggest risk today. Losing your customer is the risk," Carlson said on his YouTube show Friday.

His thesis is simple: companies that mainly make tedious or complicated tasks easier may be vulnerable if a general-purpose AI agent can do the same job itself.

"Friction is the product until a machine absorbs the friction," Carlson said.

Carlson framed the video as a rebuttal to Citrini Research’s Feb. 22 "2028 Global Intelligence Crisis," which he called "thought-provoking" but "full of flaws."

Booking, Intuit ‘Sell Friction’

Carlson said companies that "sell friction" are most exposed.

Travelers use Booking to search hotels, compare terms and make reservations. Carlson argues an AI agent could increasingly do all of that itself, creating what he calls a "gatekeeper swap."

Booking spent roughly $8.2 billion on marketing in 2025, about 30% of revenue. Carlson, a former shareholder, said he is more concerned about Booking now than when he sold it.

The concern is spreading beyond Booking. Airbnb Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) and Tripadvisor Inc. (NASDAQ:TRIP) were down more than 4% Wednesday, while Expedia Group Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE) fell as much as 6%, as investors weighed whether agents such as Meta’s Muse could take over parts of travel search and booking.

Carlson sees a similar problem for Intuit. If an agent already knows a customer’s finances and can collect documents, it could automate much of the work TurboTax currently guides users through.

Carlson said he is "far more concerned" about Intuit shareholders than when he sold the stock, arguing some of the value provided by TurboTax and Credit Karma is being "compressed."

Meta and Microsoft Could Become the Gatekeepers

Carlson argues Facebook and Instagram can still create demand even if an AI agent handles the shopping that follows. "Meta is probably more insulated from agentic threat than Google is because of the way that their advertising works," he said.

Meta also owns Muse. If people shop through it, Carlson said, Meta becomes “the new toll collector,” taking “a sliver of every transaction.”

Microsoft’s advantage, Carlson said, is workplace identity and permissions. He calls it the "agentic operating system" because its software already sits across email, documents, cloud infrastructure and security.

Microsoft says nearly 40 million agents have been registered through Agent 365.

Carlson still owns both companies and said he has been buying Meta "like crazy," calling Meta and Microsoft potential "beneficiaries" of agent technology.

On Polymarket, the AI race is still priced as a model contest. Traders give Anthropic a 70% chance of having the best AI model at year-end, compared with 2% for Meta.

Carlson said Microsoft could remain insulated from disruption "even when they don’t have their leading AI model lab," suggesting the economic winners may not need the top-ranked model.

Image: Shutterstock

news.summary: Joseph Carlson says AI agents could pressure Booking and Intuit while favoring Meta and Microsoft as customer relationships become the moat.

news.author: Chris Katje
news.content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) stock continues to soar on the heels of optimism surrounding the company’s Muse AI agent. The AI agent shares its name with a popular British rock band, which was affected by the launch.

Meta Lands Muse Social Media Handles

Meta has added more than $200 billion to its market capitalization in recent days and the stock rise has helped boost the wealth of CEO Mark Zuckerberg.

With Muse being a key product for Meta going forward, the company appears to have had its eyes set on securing the social media handles before the AI agent was publicly launched.

In a recent interview with Muse singer Matt Bellamy and iHeartRadio, the frontman said that he was sent "the beta version of the AI" ahead of the Muse launch.

Bellamy says he met with Zuckerberg.

"He’s alright, he’s not too bad," Bellamy said, as shared by NME.

Meta now owns the @Muse handle across multiple social media platforms, including X where the band is now @musetheband and on Instagram where the band is now @museband. Muse is not as active on X, but has 2.8 million followers on Instagram, compared to 185,000 for the @muse account from Meta.

Bellamy clarified that Zuckerberg and Meta didn’t "steal" the username.

"No, no. We had a chat. He invited me to meet him, and we had a chat."

The Muse singer says that there remain some trademark rules in place after giving up the social media handles.

"It’s a trademark thing. SO I said, ‘don’t touch music, don’t touch merchandise’, so I can sell Muse AI T-shirts, but I can’t make Muse AI, basically."

Some Muse fans have been surprised by the talks with Meta, given that some of the band’s lyrics reference technology taking over.

Read Also: Meta Stock ‘Has More Room to Run’: Former Hedge Fund Manager Calls It His ‘Favorite Large-Cap Tech Stock’

Taking Over Names, Social Media

Meta is not a stranger to taking over names from others in the past. The company, which was previously known as Facebook with the stock ticker FB, later changed its name to Meta Platforms and was able to secure the stock ticker META from ETF company Roundhill Investments.

On X, some of the top handles were taken over by the social media company in 2023, after Elon Musk acquired it.

This included stealing handles like @x, @music, @sports, @movies and @TV, with past owners of the handles saying they were not compensated and told they would have to pick a new handle.

Meta landing the Muse accounts likely shows that this is a product it has high hopes for.

Read Also: Meta's Muse Hits No. 1, Carrying AMD Into the $1-Trillion Club

news.headline: Meta Lands @Muse Social Media Handles: Zuckerberg Didn’t Steal From Rock Band – ‘We Had a Chat’
news.summary: Meta launched an AI product named Muse, sharing the name of a rock band. Here's how the band was involved.

Quantum Computing Breakthrough

Please click here for an enlarged chart of IONQ Inc (NYSE:IONQ).

Note the following:

  • This article is about the big picture, not an individual stock. The chart of IONQ is being used to illustrate the point of a major technological breakthrough in the important technology of quantum computing.
  • The chart shows that IONQ is in zone 1 (resistance).
  • The chart shows that IONQ stock is jumping on a major breakthrough.
  • The chart shows zone 2 (support) is far away.
  • RSI on the chart shows the stock is overbought.
  • The big, real world problem with quantum computing has been the errors. 
  • IONQ stock is jumping after IonQ demonstrated that a standard CPU could keep pace with the real time error decoding demands of simulated fault tolerant quantum workloads involving as many as 408 logical qubits and more than 31 million operations.
  • In our analysis, the breakthrough suggests that the conventional computing required to correct quantum errors may not become the major scaling bottleneck many had feared.  However, investors need to remain skeptical until more details are available.
  • There are several quantum computing technologies.  At this time, it is not known which technology will win out.
  • IonQ and Quantinuum Inc (QNT) both use trapped ion technology, in which electrically charged atoms serve as qubits and are controlled with lasers.  Trapped ion systems generally offer very high accuracy and flexible connectivity, although they operate more slowly than superconducting systems.  In this case, the slower operating cycle gave IonQ’s ordinary CPU considerably more time to decode errors.
  • The breakthrough comes as the Quantum World Congress begins today.  The congress may bring more news and more developments that can move quantum computing stocks such as IBM Common Stock (IBM), Rigetti Computing Inc (RGTI), D-Wave Quantum Inc (QBTS), Quantum Computing Inc (QUBT), and Infleqtion inc (INFQ).
  • As a full disclosure, there is a new signal on IONQ in our Buy report.
  • After a significant run starting late last week.  AI stocks are taking a breather this morning as some investors take profits.  Money flows show that the primary reason for the torrid run has been the momo crowd front running earnings season.  The first test will come when Micron Technology Inc (MU) report earnings on September 30.  As a full disclosure, we are long MU from an average of $21.77.
  • Prudent investor should note the following:
    •  When Micron reported earnings last quarter, the stock first ran up and then quickly dropped 41% intraday.
    • The drop came in spite of Micron beating earnings consensus by 20%, revenue consensus by 15%, and earnings guidance consensus by 20%.
    • In our analysis, as we previously shared, the reason MU stock fell in spite of stellar earnings was very positive positioning ahead of earnings.  When positioning is very positive, it is like everyone being on the same side of the boat.  Minor turbulence can capsize the boat.
    • In our analysis, so far positioning in MU stock this time is positive but not very positive.
    • Micron whisper numbers continue to move higher.  Stocks move based on the difference between reported numbers and whisper numbers.
  • In our analysis, it is important for investors to watch money flows, positioning, and whisper numbers on Micron as they progress to September 30.  The result will have implications for the entire AI trade, not just MU, and in turn for the entire stock market.
